The 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill marks a significant turn from the 131st Amendment Bill moved by the Centre in April 2026 that sought to redistribute Lok Sabha seats among States according to the 2011 Census population.

The proposed amendment removes the linkage of the existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats to the 1971 Census and links it with provisions related to women’s reservation in Article 334A of the Constitution.

items.title: Lok Sabha seat freeze is no longer linked to population stabilisation

The existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats was based on the population distribution recorded in the 1971 Census, and determined in the delimitation of 1973.

items.title: RBI rolls back tighter daily CRR requirement as banking liquidity slips into deficit
points: The measure will take effect from 1 December, the central bank said in a statement on Friday.
Banking system liquidity has tightened sharply, swinging from a surplus of nearly ₹11 trillion on 13 September to a deficit of ₹12,825 crore on 21 November, RBI data showed.
The last time system liquidity was in deficit was on 22 June.
As on 26 November, liquidity in the banking system was in a deficit of ₹47,641 crore.

The tighter daily maintenance requirement was introduced to absorb surplus liquidity following substantial inflows through the foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) deposit scheme, which attracted $133 billion.

items.title: SEBI clarifies 65-year age limit for stock exchange MDs remains unchanged
points: In a press release, the regulator said certain media reports and articles had misinterpreted aspects of its consultation paper titled “Strengthening the Governance of Market Infrastructure Institutions (MIIs)”, issued on November 20, 2026.
“It is further clarified that the instant consultation paper does not propose any change in the maximum age limit of 65 years applicable to the MDs of MIIs,” SEBI said.
SEBI explained that its consultation papers include proposals only for provisions where changes are intended, while those intended to remain unchanged are not included.
Under the existing framework, an MD can serve for a maximum of 10 years at a single MII, with no cumulative tenure limit across different MIIs, subject to the maximum age limit of 65 years.

In its November 20 consultation paper, SEBI proposed reducing the maximum tenure of an MD at a single MII from 10 years to eight years, while introducing a cumulative tenure cap of 12 years across MIIs.

The facility has a design capacity to produce 2 million tonnes of LNG in a year.
In 2016, Petronas launched its first floating unit, PFLNG Satu, for shallow waters, followed by the deepwater PFLNG Dua in 2021.

items.title: Mahindra Manulife opens hybrid long-short fund offer
points: The strategy plans to invest 65-75 per cent in equity and equity-related instruments, including arbitrage positions Mahindra Manulife Mutual Fund has launched the MSIF Hybrid Long-Short Fund, an interval investment strategy that invests in equity and debt…
It is offered under the fund house’s Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) platform, MSIF.
The New Fund Offer opens on 27 November 2026 and closes on 11 December 2026.
Continuous sale and repurchase will begin on 21 December 2026.

The fund may take unhedged short positions of up to 25 per cent of net assets, use option strategies within regulatory limits, and participate in special situations such as IPOs, buybacks, mergers and demergers.
Anthony Heredia, MD and CEO of Mahindra Manulife Investment Management, said the fund combines fixed income and arbitrage with long and short equity positions.
Krishna Sanghavi, Chief Investment Officer (Equity), said short positions will follow the same research discipline as long positions.

items.title: CDS General Subramani flags Pakistan’s space growth with China, Turkey’s help: ‘Must factor it into our calculus’
points: Pakistan's expanding space capabilities, backed by China and Turkey, have added a new dimension to India’s security calculus, Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani said on Friday, underscoring the need for the country to strengthen its own space…
"Pakistan's space capability is improving with Chinese help.
Also, Pakistan's Suparco (Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission) is working to develop its own capability.
Subramani's comments come against the backdrop of closer military cooperation among Pakistan, China and Turkey, which came into focus during Operation Sindoor last year.

Spearheaded by the Defence Space Agency under the HQ Integrated Defence Staff, the ₹26,968-crore project involves ISRO constructing and launching 21 satellites, with private companies handling the remaining 31.
The official's remarks came days after Pakistani air force pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the first foreign astronaut to blast off China's Shenzhou-24 spacecraft to the Tiangong space station.
China on Wednesday launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts, two Chinese and a Pakistani.

items.title: Japan’s First Ammonia-Fuelled Car Carriers Set To Cross The Pacific On Ammonia Alone By 2030
points: Japan’s first four ammonia-fuelled car carriers will be equipped with ammonia fuel handling systems from Mitsubishi Shipbuilding.
The shipbuilder’s parent company Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) announced the selection on November 26, 2026, but did not disclose the value of the contract.
Mitsubishi Shipbuilding will supply its Mitsubishi Ammonia Supply and Safety System (MAmmoSS) for the vessels and also prepare the basic design of their ammonia fuel tanks.
The four ships are scheduled for completion in 2030 and will be operated by Nippon Yusen Kabushiki Kaisha (NYK Line) and Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha (K Line), with two vessels each.
Each of the ammonia-fuelled car carriers will be fitted with dual-fuel engines, and its tanks will hold sufficient fuel to cross the Pacific Ocean using only ammonia.
The basic design work for the ships will be led by Shin Kurushima Dockyard, which will share the construction with Imabari Shipbuilding and Nihon Shipyard.

items.title: South Korea’s Hanwha Ocean Exits $4.1 Billion 800 MW Offshore Wind Project
points: Hanwha Ocean has decided to exit the 800 MW Southwest Offshore Wind Expansion Complex 1 project, which is being planned in South Korea’s Jeonbuk Province.
The South Korean shipbuilder announced its final decision through a regulatory disclosure on November 25, 2026, after reviewing the related circumstances.

Despite exiting this project, Hanwha Ocean remains active in the offshore wind sector, building specialised wind turbine installation vessels and developing other wind farms off South Korea’s coast, including the 390 MW Shinan Ui project.
Hanwha Ocean was among the members of a consortium led by Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power (KHNP) which had been chosen as the preferred bidder in June 2026.
As per the tender rules, public institutions had to hold a combined stake of at least 50% in the project.
The wind farm will come up in the waters off Buan County in Jeonbuk Province, and for the same reason it is also called the Buan 800 MW offshore wind farm.

items.title: Volkswagen To Court During Import Duty Evasion Case: Mercedes, Kia & BMW Doing The Same
points: Volkswagen has told an Indian court that manufacturers such as Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Kia also import car components at the lower 10% customs duty rate, just as it does.

The German carmaker argues that Indian tax authorities are unfairly targeting it with the $1.2 billion (around Rs 11,154 crore rupees) tax demand while allowing other manufacturers to follow a similar import model.
In a court filing dated November 10, 2026, Volkswagen's Indian subsidiary, Skoda Auto Volkswagen India, disputed the tax authorities' claim that it was the only manufacturer using this import method.
The company said other manufacturers of comparable vehicles also import components under the lower 10% duty category.
To support its argument, Volkswagen submitted a table showing import shipment figures for Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Kia, Isuzu and JSW MG Motor, the Indian joint venture involving China's SAIC Motor.
According to the filing, BMW recorded 390,360 major component import shipments in 2024, while Mercedes-Benz recorded 80,972.

items.title: UN Expects No Growth In Global Maritime Trade For 2026 After 95% Drop In Hormuz Traffic
points: Global maritime trade is expected to record zero growth in 2026 as conflicts and disruptions at key shipping chokepoints push vessels onto longer routes.
Over 80% of global trade shipping delays disrupt everyday supplies of food, fuel, and consumer goods.
UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) gave the forecast in its Review of Maritime Transport 2026 report, which was released on November 26.
Seaborne trade reached 12.3 billion tons in 2025 after growing by 1.9%, which was well below the 3.9% growth recorded in 2024.
The UN body expects global maritime trade to recover by 3.2% in 2027 after stalling this year.
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has dropped sharply since the Middle East conflict began in late February 2026.
The global fleet grew its cargo-carrying capacity by 3.5% in 2025, which outpaced trade growth, but 42% of all vessels are more than 20 years old.
Scheduled container capacity rose by 53% at Mundra port and 47% at Nhava Sheva port in India between February and June 2026.

items.title: Iran Claims LNG Tanker Caught Fire After Hitting Naval Mine In Strait Of Hormuz
points: An LNG tanker caught fire after it hit a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz on November 25, claims Iran’s Revolutionary Guards.

As per the statement of the Revolutionary Guards Navy which was carried by Iranian media, the tanker had turned off its detection and navigation systems and entered the ‘prohibited area’ even after getting warnings.
Commercial vessels carry Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponders that broadcast their location to nearby ships and coastal authorities.
The vessel then hit a naval mine and caught fire, after which it came to a standstill in the waterway.
He added that ships which pass through the strait without coordinating with the Iranian forces have faced greater risks and hit mines in the past few weeks.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) also received a report of an unknown projectile exploding near a tanker 50 nautical miles west of Dubai.

items.title: Saudi Arabia’s Jazan Port Damaged In Houthi Strike As Red Sea Ports Face Attack Threats
points: Jazan port in southwestern Saudi Arabia was struck by a projectile fired by Yemen’s Houthi group on November 25, the Saudi-led coalition said.
On the same day, a Houthi drone was shot down by Saudi-led forces in the area near Jeddah Islamic Port.
Jeddah Islamic Port is Saudi Arabia’s busiest maritime hub on the Red Sea and handles the bulk of the kingdom’s commercial cargo and container traffic.
Saudi air defences also intercepted at least one Houthi missile while Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence issued a danger alert for Riyadh province, which was later lifted.
A day before these strikes, 11 people were hurt when the Houthis attacked a tower located in the King Abdullah Financial District of Riyadh.
Saudi Red Sea ports such as Jeddah were named as targets by the Houthis, who had warned of strikes in case the coalition went after Hodeidah port in Yemen.
The attacks on Jazan port and Jeddah are part of an escalating Houthi campaign against Saudi airports, oil facilities and other infrastructure.

items.title: Oppo Tipped to Launch Three Wide-Screen Phones in 2027 Across Flagship, Mid-Range Segments
points: Oppo was previously rumoured to be working on a wide-format phone, which was expected to launch under the Reno X branding.

Oppo recently launched the Find X10 series in India comprising two models Oppo is said to be preparing to expand its smartphone lineup with multiple devices featuring a wider-than-usual candybar design.
According to a tipster, the company is developing three such phones for 2027, spanning its flagship and mid-range offerings.
One of the upcoming models is tipped to feature a 6.35-inch display and a MediaTek Dimensity 9-series chipset, while another could focus on photography in a slimmer and lighter body.
In a Weibo post, tipster Digital Chat Station (translated from Chinese) claims that Oppo has three wide candybar smartphones in its plans for 2027.
The first smartphone is said to belong to Oppo's flagship Find series and feature a 6.35-inch display.
As per the tipster, the third model is reportedly planned for the end of 2027 and is expected to succeed the first flagship wide phone.

items.title: ‘Acted at dictates of political bosses’: SC talks tough after Deepathoon order violated in Tamil Nadu
points: The Supreme Court on Friday came down heavily on the Tamil Nadu government and temple authorities over the failure to implement its November 20 order permitting the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the disputed stone pillar or ‘Deepathoon’ on…
“The chain of events that has unfolded in the instant case would indicate that the executive authorities seem to have acted at the dictates of their political bosses.

The same has to be unearthed not only to save the dignity of this Court but also to maintain purity in the administration of justice." a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi said, according to LiveLaw.
The SC bench observed that the conduct of officials prima facie revealed a state of “administrative chaos” in Tamil Nadu, or “at least” specifically in the Madurai district, Bar and Bench reported.
The bench has directed the chief secretary to appear before it on December 15 and file an affidavit detailing communications between officials in connection with implementation of the order.

items.title: 55-year-old neighbour molests 6-year-old girl in Faridabad; booked under POCSO after victim's mother files complaint
points: A six-year-old girl was allegedly molested by a neighbour here, with police registering a POCSO case and launching a search to nab the absconding accused, officials said on Friday.

It is alleged that a 55-year-old neighbour grabbed the girl while she was playingin the street outside her home, located under Dabua police station area, and began engaging in obscene acts with her, police said.
During this, the girl's mother arrived at the scene and witnessed the incident, forcing the accused to flee.
On the mother's complaint, a case was registered under provisions of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act at Dabua police station, officials said.
According to the complaint, the girl was playing in the street outside their home on Wednesday night.

During this, the accused, who lived in the same neighbourhood, allegedly approached the child, grabbed her and engaged in inappropriate acts with her, before her mother arrived and caught him in the act.
"An FIR under the POCSO Act has been registered.

items.title: 22-year-old Keralam woman found dead at lodge in Bengaluru; boyfriend suspected of murder
points: A 22-year-old woman was found dead at a lodge in Bengaluru's Cottonpete area on Friday, with her boyfriend suspected to be involved in the murder, police said.
The incident was reported at a lodge on OTC Road, near Thawakal Mastan Dargah, within the limits of Cottonpete Police Station.
The suspected accused, a 23-year-old man also from Keralam, had completed a BSc Nursing course and worked in arranging admissions for nursing aspirants in nursing colleges.
The incident took place at the lodge on Friday at around 11 am.
A murder case has been registered at Cottonpete Police Station under Crime No. 251/26 under the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
A case has been registered at Banashankari Police Station in Crime No. 236/2026 under Sections 103(1) and 109(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) - 2023.
According to the complaint, he had rented out the flat to Seema Das and her family from October 3, 2024.

items.title: CERT-In Warns WhatsApp Users of ‘High-Severity’ Vulnerabilities Across Android, iOS, and Desktop
points: CERT-In highlighted multiple security flaws in several WhatsApp products developed by Meta.

Meta said it had not seen evidence of the first vulnerability being exploited in the wild The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has issued an advisory regarding multiple vulnerabilities affecting WhatsApp across various devices and…
All individual users and organisations using WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business on mobile devices, as well as WhatsApp for Mac Desktop, have been advised to take note of the security risk.
In its vulnerability note CIVN-2026-0576, issued on November 26, CERT-In highlighted multiple security flaws in several WhatsApp products developed by Meta.
The first, tracked as CVE-2026-102769, is a SQL injection flaw in WhatsApp for Android versions before 2.26.35.74.
The third flaw, CVE-2026-23871, affects WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Android versions before 2.26.17.4.
To mitigate the risks, both CERT-In and WhatsApp have advised users to ensure that WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business are updated to the latest available versions through their respective app stores.

points: Oppo Pad 6 F Lite has been listed on Oppo's website in Romania, confirming its imminent launch in select global markets.
It will be available for purchase via the company website in a single Frost Silver colourway and the sole 4GB + 128GB RAM and storage configuration.

items.title: E-certificates for new citizens, hard copy on request
points: Individuals acquiring Indian citizenship will receive a digital certificate instead of a physical copy.
This change applies to those registered or naturalised as citizens.
Applicants can request a hard copy if desired, as per the new amendments.
The digital certificates will be signed by an authorized officer from the central government.
These amendments aim to modernize the process of issuing citizenship certificates in India.

items.title: Supreme Court junks plea seeking its intervention to remove Italian politician’s ‘vote chor’ remark on socials
points: The Supreme Court of India dismissed a plea concerning Giacomo Filibeck's remarks made during the Bharat Summit.
The court stated that the petitioner could represent concerns to the Centre regarding regulations on foreign speeches.
Filibeck's slogan and comments on Rahul Gandhi sparked controversy within political spaces.
Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh emphasized the right to file complaints.

points: Authorities are investigating gangster Ravi Rathi's suspected role in a shocking quadruple murder tied to his rival, Sunny Ritoli.
Operating from Georgia, Rathi's henchmen employed a honeytrap to bait Ritoli into a lethal ambush at a hotel, resulting in the deaths of three aides while Ritoli narrowly escaped.
Investigative teams are intensifying efforts to pinpoint Rathi's whereabouts, bracing for any retaliation as tensions escalate following the attack on Ritoli's crew.

Many of these complaints were supported by documentary evidence, which adds credibility to the claims.
Complaints against Justice Prasad also reached Chief Minister Hemant Soren, who urged CJI Kant to address these concerns.
Justice Prasad has held his position since 2014 but could face scrutiny due to the complaints received.

points: In a significant ruling, the Supreme Court has reprimanded Tamil Nadu officials for their willful defiance of judicial orders.
The court has now permitted all devotees to light lamps at the controversial location, expressing serious concern over the state's non-compliance and the initiation of contempt proceedings.
Additionally, former judges have been appointed to supervise temple matters, reinforcing the importance of adhering to the rule of law.

points: B R Gavai expressed his apprehension regarding the Supreme Court's suggestion to transfer Justice M S Ramachandra Rao.
Citing Rao's previous punitive transfers, Gavai questioned the wisdom in elevating a judge from a lesser high court to a more significant position.
He warned that such actions could demoralize diligent judges within the judiciary, drawing from his own experiences in the collegium.

points: Ex-CJI B R Gavai has sharply criticized the current Supreme Court Collegium for ignoring diversity in judicial appointments.

His letter to President Droupadi Murmu urged accountability for these practices in the selection process.
Gavai emphasized the need for proportional representation of marginalized communities in the judiciary.

points: The Union Cabinet has given the green light to a new bill aimed at expanding the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats.
This legislation introduces a significant milestone—a one-third reservation for women in both the Lok Sabha and state assemblies, set to commence in 2029.
Additionally, it proposes a uniform 50% increase in constituencies across all states, based on the 2011 Census.

items.title: Bisleri in fresh trouble, after Goa FSSAI finds bacteria in West Bengal water sample
points: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has initiated prosecution against Bisleri International over unsafe drinking water samples.
Recent tests revealed coliform bacteria in samples from its West Bengal and Goa plants.
FSSAI has restricted the sale of specific batches following these findings and intensified surveillance on packaged drinking water quality.
The regulator aims to ensure compliance with food safety norms across the country.

items.title: Mirwaiz under house arrest after Sheshnag, Vande Mataram criticism; barred from leading Friday prayers
points: J&K administration has placed Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, chairman of the Hurriyat Conference, under house arrest, hindering his ability to lead significant Friday prayers at Jamia Masjid.
This move follows his outspoken criticism of recent construction near Sheshnag Lake and the ongoing controversy surrounding the song Vande Mataram, which has raised religious concerns.
PDP president Mehbooba Mufti and others have criticized this decision, citing restrictions on religious expression.

items.title: J&K gets advocate general after 2 years
points: Syed Faisal Qadri has been appointed the advocate general of Jammu & Kashmir, filling a key role.
This important position remained vacant for two years due to administrative differences following a change in government.
An additional advocate general had been handling responsibilities during this period of vacancy.
A public interest litigation highlighted the adverse effects of this prolonged absence on legal governance.

points: Vehicle owners face hefty fines for masking or tampering with registration numbers.
In a move to curb toll evasion, the Road Transport Ministry has instructed NHAI to enforce stringent penalties.
